description: A request rejected during a refresh starts a second one
old:
ELSE IF inflight > 0
       THEN /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![k].phase = "waiting", ![k].again = TRUE]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, usedRt, sends>>
new:
ELSE IF inflight > 0
       THEN /\ req' = [req EXCEPT ![k].phase = "waiting", ![k].again = TRUE]
            /\ inflight' = inflight + 1 /\ usedRt' = rt /\ UNCHANGED sends

description: A rotated refresh token isn't kept
old: /\ rt' = IF rotate THEN gen + 1 ELSE rt

description: A rejected request goes out again with the same token
A second rejection sends the request yet again
A request close to expiry waits without starting a refresh
A failed refresh leaves the requests waiting
A sign-in replaces the refresh but leaves the requests waiting
old:
/\ inflight' = 0
    /\ req' = Release("sent")
    /\ sends' = Released("sent")
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deadRt, usedRt, rejectedG>>
new:
/\ inflight' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<req, sends, deadRt, usedRt, rejectedG>>

description: The authorization server need not answer a refresh
A refusal that names an error is read as a passing failure, so the tokens are kept and the dead refresh token is sent again (Slack's HTTP-200 ok:false)
old:
/\ held' = FALSE
    /\ refreshable' = FALSE
    /\ inflight' = 0
    /\ req' = [k \in Keys |-> IF req[k].phase = "waiting" THEN [req[k] EXCEPT !.phase = "needs_sign_in"] ELSE req[k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, rt, valid, serverRt, usedRt, sends, rejectedG>>
new:
/\ inflight' = 0
    /\ req' = [k \in Keys |-> IF req[k].phase = "waiting" THEN [req[k] EXCEPT !.phase = "failed"] ELSE req[k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, held, refreshable, rt, valid, serverRt, usedRt, sends, rejectedG>>
